::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What is the shortest distance from the ellipse $x^2+\frac{y^2}{4} =1$ and the point (2,2).](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/3635723/what-is-the-shortest-distance-from-the-ellipse-x2-fracy24-1-and-the-po), asked by [kt046172](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/604278/kt046172) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2020-04-21; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> What is the shortest distance from the ellipse $x^2+\frac{y^2}{4} =1$ and the point (2,2).
>
> I know that this is the projection of (2,2) onto the ellipse. How do I go about finding the shortest distance between this point and the curve?
:::

You can think about this as a constrained optimization problem.  You want to minimize the function $f(x,y) = (x-2)^2 + (y-2)^2$ [the square of the distance from $(x,y)$ to $(2,2)$], subject to the constraint that $x^2+y^2/4=1$.
